## Appearance

Opal Pettigrew is described as the most beautiful girl at the [Academy](../codex/places.md#regent-s-academy), possessing a striking appearance with big, vivid blue eyes, radiant skin, and a good complexion. While initially noted for her full and eye-catching shape, she later becomes extremely slender, with fragile, nearly see-through hands. Her long blonde hair, which she has worn in a lengthy plait, can also be seen adorned with red geraniums.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Regent’s Class Is Organized P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Regent’s P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. ## Personality

Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny and pleasant disposition, openly delighting in life and showing a strong tendency toward laughter and sentimentality, though she is also prone to hysteria. Her focus is heavily consumed by romance, boys, and receiving male compliments. From a young age, her ambitions revolve around courtship: she intends to secure a boyfriend at age fifteen, keep numerous suitors dangling to drive them wild, and enjoy a vibrant social life before teaching for two years and eventually marrying. On a personal level, she harbors intense fears of plump green caterpillars and of lying flat to feign death on a floating craft. She also expresses a deep desire to continue living, terrified that the afterlife will feel foreign and make her homesick.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. ## History

Opal Pettigrew grew up with a large number of older sisters who were quickly married off, and she expressed a childhood ambition to have dozens of suitors as an adult. During her youth, she attended school and Regent's alongside [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md), and she once cured her warts using an enchanted stone from old [Mary Joe](../character/mary-joe.md). Hideaway in a hallway pantry, she overheard her sister [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) receive a marriage proposal. After visiting [Boston](../codex/places.md#boston) one autumn, Opal received a marriage proposal from Nelson Atkins, but she returned home and wrote him a blistering rejection. Later, after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) returned to [Brierley](../codex/places.md#brierley), she learned that Opal had become gravely ill with consumption. Sitting together in the garden, Opal tearfully confessed to [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) her fear of dying and her unfulfilled desires for her life, after which she passed away peacefully in her sleep.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018), [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. ## Quotes

> "It fills me with fear, girls. Is it really proper for us to perform in this manner, do you think? Mrs. Sowerby claims that any drama-acting is dreadfully sinful."
>
> — Opal Pettigrew — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013)

> "Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!"
>
> — Opal Pettigrew — [v3 ch.Summons P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)

> "I will endeavor to do so. What you told me will be weighed in my mind, and I will attempt to hold it as true. Also, your visits will be as frequent as possible, will they not, Nell?"
>
> — Opal Pettigrew — [v3 ch.Summons P21](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0021)

> "I am aware. Already, you have provided aid to me. At present, nothing appears entirely so terrible. Good night, Nell."
>
> — Opal Pettigrew — [v3 ch.Summons P27](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0027)

> "I am pleased that I have shared this with you, Nell,"
>
> — Opal Pettigrew — [v3 ch.Summons P19](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0019)
